title: Vietnamese phin brewing guide
scope: Nguyen Coffee Supply single-serving 4 oz stainless steel gravity phin with a loose drop-in disc; explicit rounded metric volume adaptation, not a universal screw-phin recipe

sources.title: Phin Filter: traditional Vietnamese drip guide
supports: 14 g dose; 4 oz water; 1 oz initial pour and 45-second wait; 195–200 F; disc before wetting; serving options
Printed 1:2 lacks a common-unit definition and is not a verified mass ratio

sources.title: Dialing In Your Phin: How to Make the Best Vietnamese Phin Coffee
supports: Single-serving 4 oz phin scope; first drip by two minutes and last near five
Finer grind slows flow; loose gravity-disc lift and release can restore gas-stalled flow

sources.title: How to Use & Clean a Vietnamese Phin Filter
supports: Dry parts and soft washing; avoid abrasives; dishwasher permission for this maker's phins
Alternative insert-after-bloom troubleshooting technique; timing is not a strict pass/fail rule

sources.title: Phin Filter FAQ: Every Question Answered
supports: Stainless steel brewer, separate gravity disc, plate, chamber and lid; no paper; lid as coaster
Water and soap cleaning; fine grind and sufficient dose for the 4 oz size; dilution and serving are optional

sources.title: Phin Filter (Black)
supports: A different 8 oz aluminum phin with recommended hand washing; dishwasher permission must not be generalized

sources.title: Cà Phê Rang Xay Trung Nguyên Legend Thiên product declaration and packaging
supports: PDF identified as a 15-page original manufacturer document; recipe text was unavailable and the requested page screenshot timed out; no recipe claim relies on it

recipe.name: 4 oz gravity phin: rounded metric volume adaptation
equipment: Nguyen Coffee Supply 4 oz stainless steel gravity phin with its loose disc, plate, chamber and lid
Stable heat-safe cup supporting the plate
recipe.grind_description: Fine, with visible sand-like particles; dial to this phin rather than a universal grinder number

expected_time_s.clock_start: Initial water first touches coffee; app-authored clock convention because source does not state origin
expected_time_s.clock_end: Standing water has drained and dripping ends; around 300 seconds is a reference, not a forced stop

recipe.completion_signal: No standing brew water remains and dripping has ended; first drip is an earlier diagnostic cue
adaptation_notes: Interpret the US roaster's ounces of water as US fluid ounces, not ounces by mass
4 US fl oz is approximately 118.3 ml, rounded to 118 ml; 1 US fl oz is approximately 29.6 ml, rounded to 30 ml; remaining volume is 88 ml
195–200 F is approximately 90.6–93.3 C; selected metric range is 91–93 C
Do not read the source's printed 1:2 as a grams-to-grams ratio

steps.instruction: Use clean dry parts; seat the plate and chamber firmly on a stable heat-safe cup.
steps.why: Clear holes and stable support prevent blocked flow and spills.
steps.completion: Holes are clean; brewer sits flat without rocking.

steps.instruction: Add 14 g coffee, gently level it, and rest the loose disc flat on top without compressing.
steps.why: The bed is even and the insert remains free to rise.
steps.completion: Level coffee bed with a freely resting disc.

steps.instruction: Start timing at first water contact, gently add 30 ml, and wait until the timer reads 45 seconds.
steps.why: The bed wets and begins swelling before the main fill.
steps.completion: Coffee has absorbed the initial pour and begun swelling.

steps.instruction: Add 88 ml more, keeping below the rim; allow drainage if needed to finish the measured pour, then cover.
steps.why: Complete the chosen volume without overflowing the chamber.
steps.completion: 118 ml total added without overflow; lid is on.

steps.instruction: Observe the first drip, then wait for drainage and the last drops.
steps.why: First flow and completion are separate cues; elapsed time guides diagnosis.
steps.completion: Water has drained and dripping ends; reference first drip by about 120 seconds and completion near 300 seconds.

steps.instruction: Protect hands from hot metal, remove the phin onto its inverted lid or heat-safe tray, and serve.
steps.why: Separate brewer removal from optional dilution, condensed milk or ice.
steps.completion: Phin is supported safely and coffee is ready for the chosen serving.

variants.name: Optional condensed milk or iced serving
variants.how_it_differs: Keep extraction unchanged; stir milk into collected coffee and add ice separately. No fixed milk, dilution or ice quantity is established by this baseline.

variants.name: Alternative gravity-disc bloom order
variants.how_it_differs: Nguyen's care article suggests initial wetting before inserting the disc for stalled brews. This is a different procedure from the traditional guide followed here, not an instruction to switch order mid-brew.

variants.name: Different phin size or material
variants.how_it_differs: Select a model-specific recipe and care instructions; Nam's 8 oz aluminum phin recommends hand washing. Do not automatically scale this 4 oz example.

variants.name: Screw or slot-lock insert
variants.how_it_differs: Requires model-specific assembly and recipe evidence; a loose gravity-disc procedure does not validate threaded adjustment or a supplier's slot-lock procedure. No exact screw recipe is established here.

troubleshooting.check_first: Clean holes, dry parts, correct seating and an uncompressed loose disc.
troubleshooting.adjustment: For this gravity disc only, safely lift and release it briefly with a utensil to vent gas; otherwise let it cool. If the next brew still stalls, grind slightly coarser.

troubleshooting.check_first: Confirm measured coffee dose, flat disc and even bed.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Try a slightly finer grind next brew with water and dose unchanged.

troubleshooting.check_first: Taste before adding milk or ice and confirm the input volume.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Dilute the collected coffee to taste, recording that water separately from extraction.

troubleshooting.symptom: Harsh or sour despite reasonable drainage
troubleshooting.check_first: Check temperature and the chosen bean/roast; timing alone is not a diagnosis.
troubleshooting.adjustment: Compare one controlled change next brew; begin with a small temperature or grind adjustment within this equipment's usable range.

safety: Place the complete brewer on a level surface and a heat-safe cup that fully supports the plate before pouring.
Keep water below the rim; do not force a full chamber to accept the remaining pour.
Chamber, plate, lid and disc become hot; use heat protection and keep hands out of the water path.
A gravity disc rests loosely; never push down or squeeze to force flow, and do not transfer its venting technique to threaded hardware.
Let parts cool before removing grounds; wash with soap and a soft sponge, rinse and dry; avoid abrasive pads and steel wool.
Follow the actual brewer's cleaning instructions; Nguyen's dishwasher permission does not cover Nam's aluminum model or all phins.

app_audit.finding: Gravity recipe stores 14 g / 118 g, 8.43 mass ratio and 91–96 C with ORIGINAL_CREATOR_RECIPE/HIGH attribution. Current Nguyen water is in ounces by volume and temperature is 195–200 F; mass conversion and upper temperature are adaptations.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Preserve volume with an explicit unit basis or label a deliberately chosen mass-based adaptation; align temperature to source and downgrade exact-creator attribution accordingly.

app_audit.finding: Typed gravity stages encode 30 g plus 88 g, cumulative 118 g, and 91–96 C; first drip is no later than 120 s and finish is approximate 300 s. The observational time distinction is sound; the water unit is an unlabeled adaptation.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Correct water units and temperature consistently with catalog and live guidance; retain observation-based completion instead of forcing a timer deadline.

app_audit.finding: No phin erratum exists. P1ExactGuidanceCatalog applies this file to recipe and stage data, so the immutable p1_exact_guidance_2026_07_27.json currently supplies creator attribution and mass-based water wording to live guidance.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Add a reviewed runtime provenance/unit correction for phin; preserve the immutable historical source projection.

app_audit.finding: Historical audit says 14 g / 118 g and a 30 g bloom match the source, while acknowledging 4 oz water. Current source says initial 1 oz, not 30 g; the historical verdict does not resolve the volume/mass mismatch.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Record this later correction and its date; do not rely on the old match verdict as current unit proof.

app_audit.finding: Generic phin default is 1:5 input-water mass ratio, 90–96 C, 180–360 s and CollectedConcentrate(retainedWaterGPerCoffeeG=0.0). BrewingCatalog.kt:389 repeats zero retention; Recipe.kt:242 uses it to estimate concentrate as full brew input when no target is supplied.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Treat 1:5 as an explicit generic starting point, separate from the named Nguyen recipe; use measured output or an unresolved estimate instead of asserting zero retention.

app_audit.finding: 18 g / 120 g screw-insert profile has BATTLE_TESTED/MEDIUM status. Its Dragon Coffee URL is a supplier's spoon-dose, slot-lock insert, fill-to-level procedure, not a verified threaded-screw manufacturer procedure or those exact numeric quantities. No physical test evidence was found in this research pass.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Identify an exact threaded model and primary procedure; label existing quantities as an app-authored profile and avoid claiming battle testing without test provenance.

app_audit.finding: Production readiness already retains BLOCK-PHIN-PRIMARY-HARDWARE-EVIDENCE for phin_screw_18_120. This research confirms that exact primary hardware/recipe evidence is still unresolved.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Keep the existing blocker until model-specific primary evidence is reviewed; this guide does not clear it or establish release readiness.

app_audit.finding: No phin everyday enum entry exists. Generic profile and two exact-catalog recipes do exist; P1BuiltInGuidanceCatalog uses equipment-specific assembly and observed drainage. grinders.json has no dedicated phin target.
app_audit.change_recommendation: Describe current support as generic profile/exact catalog. Future everyday support must include hardware-sensitive defaults, unit semantics and localized content rather than claiming catalog presence covers the whole flow.

supplemental_audit_evidence.title: Dragon Coffee: Brewing Information
supplemental_audit_evidence.classification: Supplier's own procedure; secondary for Trung Nguyen manufacturer attribution
supplemental_audit_evidence.supports: The recipe specifies a slot/indentation locking disc, three rounded teaspoons, about 20 ml pre-wet for 20 seconds, then near-top fill; this is not direct evidence for a threaded 18 g/120 g recipe

uncertainties: Nguyen's printed 1:2 or FAQ 2:1 does not establish a dimensionless mass ratio beside 14 g / 4 oz; this guide uses the explicit dose and water volume, with the US-fluid-ounce interpretation stated.
The source says fill to the top without establishing usable chamber headroom with this bed; keep below the rim and allow drainage if required by the measured-volume adaptation.
Source timing origin is unstated; initial wetting is the app-authored clock convention. Approximate finish is not a hard 300-second window.
Traditional and care pages differ on disc-before versus disc-after-bloom order; this baseline follows traditional order consistently.

The Trung Nguyen Thien manufacturer PDF opened as 15 pages without extracted text, but its recipe screenshot timed out; the 2025 Chat Tien Phong manufacturer PDF also timed out. No recipe quantities are treated as verified from either.

Exact screw-thread hardware, 18 g/120 g recipe, 25 g pre-wet and 5–8-minute timing lack verified manufacturer/original-creator support in this pass; the variant is not a validated baseline and the existing production release blocker remains open.
No physical brew, localization review, Android device execution or release validation was performed; measured beverage yield and usable capacity with grounds remain untested.
do_not_claim: Water volume in milliliters equals exact mass in grams.
The printed 1:2 is a grams-to-grams coffee/water ratio.
118 ml input produces 118 g concentrate or any universal beverage yield.
Every phin has the same capacity, insert mechanics, grind or completion time.
A threaded disc or twist-lock disc uses the loose gravity-disc venting technique.
A source supplier's slot-lock guide verifies a screw-thread manufacturer recipe.
All phins are dishwasher safe, or a reviewed exact catalog establishes full everyday/localized support.
